frank: Heads-up — the "Next Launchpad" sample (LlamaIndex + eval harness) is producing different eval scores between the TS starter and the python reference.

elaine: Different how?

frank: Same dataset, same prompts, but TS run has much lower doc-recall. Looks like embeddings differ.

peter: Could be chunking or normalization differences. Any repro?

frank: Minimal repro in template:
```js
// server/ingest.js
const chunks = splitText(doc, { chunkSize: 512 });
await client.embedMany(chunks);
```
TS uses embedNormalization=false by default in @redwood/sdk, python client normalizes.

ryan: That would change nearest-neighbor ranking. We should align defaults and add a migration note.

elaine: Also saw subtle tokenization mismatch for CJK text due to different whitespace handling in the starter splitter.

peter: Action: add an e2e eval test comparing TS vs Python embeddings on a small seed dataset, and set SDK parity flags: normalizeEmbeddings=true and a shared splitter config.

frank: I'll open PR to update starter and add a short "Embedding parity" note in README so onboarding tutorials don't confuse users.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch fix/llamaindex-embedding-parity  3 checks running.

ryan: Thanks. This will reduce churn for folks following the python guides.
